It does not allocate global addresses or provide confidentiality by itself; those are functions of address configuration and security protocols. Clients still use link-layer addresses to exchange frames on the wireless link. The concrete addresses in the case do not change the rule.
questions.hint: Ask what the device connects on each side of the link.
questions.learningObjective: identify and explain a wireless access point using a packet-level scenario

options.text: An access point replaces the need for a link-layer address on clients.
options.misconception: believes wireless clients need no MAC address

options.text: An access point assigns public addresses to hosts everywhere on the Internet.
options.misconception: treats a local device as a global address authority

options.text: An access point bridges a wireless local network to a wired network and manages associations with client devices.
An access point encrypts every packet before it enters the Internet.
options.misconception: confuses local bridging with end-to-end encryption
